meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty-five minutes. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, Hale, and was Owen heard before it went in?
I don't have time for this. The zero stands.

You asked for this meeting, Hale. "The zero stands" isn't an answer: on what basis, and was Owen heard before it went into the gradebook? Answer that, or I'm in the principal's office at 4:40 instead of on my call.
Sorry. That came out wrong. Let me show you what I actually have: the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet, and his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions.

I'm writing down October 15. Show me the exact line in Owen's essay, and the outline with his name and that date on it. An outline is a plan, Hale; students change their argument all the time, so what else do you have?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require that the zero on Owen's essay be withdrawn, that Owen be heard before any decision about his mark, and that I see the essay line and the outline you described today. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, with nothing agreed; she still wants the zero withdrawn and to see the two documents you described.
What moved her: "his October 15 outline argued cowardice", because it was dated, tied to Owen's own work, and something she could check, so she started taking notes and asking real questions.
What cost ground: "The zero stands.", because it refused her question about who decided and whether Owen was heard, and pushed her toward the principal.
Try next time: in your first reply, own in one sentence that the zero went in before anyone called home, then put the outline and the essay line on screen so she can read them herself.
